benchmarks.name: ScanNet++ Benchmark
benchmarks.task: 3D semantic and instance segmentation on high-fidelity indoor scans.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Current public pages default to v2. Semantic segmentation evaluates the top 100 semantic classes, with top-1/top-3 multilabel IoU on decimated mesh vertices; instance segmentation uses the countable subset of those classes and AP/AP50/AP25. Preserve version, task, split and supervision when comparing methods.
unresolved_entries: Beyond Context Bias: Adaptive Instance Placement for Robust 3D Instance Segmentation (Rongkun Yang et al.; leaderboard row did not supply a publication URL). A primary project page and code repository exist, but this bounded import intentionally omits it pending a canonical paper record.
Anonymous instance-segmentation submissions have not been mapped to publications.

benchmarks.name: ScanNet Benchmark
benchmarks.task: Indoor 3D semantic and instance segmentation.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: State semantic, instance, or panoptic task and split for every comparison.

benchmarks.name: ScanNet200
benchmarks.task: Long-tail 3D semantic and instance segmentation with 200 classes.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Scores are not interchangeable with ScanNet20; preserve label set and metric.

benchmarks.name: S3DIS
benchmarks.task: Indoor point-cloud semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Keep Area 5 and 6-fold protocols distinct.
unresolved_entries: No single official all-method leaderboard was confirmed in this pass.

benchmarks.name: MultiScan Benchmark
benchmarks.task: Object instance segmentation, part instance segmentation, and mobility prediction in articulated indoor environments.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Official repository exposes separate benchmark downloads and data preparation paths for object, part, and mobility tasks.

benchmarks.name: ARKitScenes
benchmarks.task: Mobile RGB-D indoor scene understanding tasks.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Access and download are governed by the dataset repository and its terms; do not equate its task protocols with ScanNet.

benchmarks.name: Articulation-XL2.0
benchmarks.task: Static 3D assets to articulated structure and motion.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Official MagicArticulate release links the data; no canonical public leaderboard was verified.

benchmarks.name: PartNet-Mobility
benchmarks.task: Articulated object assets, motion annotations, rendering, and simulation.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Use paper-specific protocols; this is not a cross-paper leaderboard.

benchmarks.name: Articulated Container Dataset
benchmarks.task: Openable containers with articulation annotations.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: PAct evaluates on ACD; a canonical public leaderboard was not located in this pass.

benchmarks.name: ManiSkill2
benchmarks.task: Generalizable manipulation with articulated tasks including cabinet doors/drawers, faucets, chairs, mobile-base and dual-arm settings.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Scores require task, observation modality, embodiment, controller, and split. The public ongoing leaderboard is benchmark-specific; this survey should ingest results only with those fields.

benchmarks.name: RLBench
benchmarks.task: Vision-guided manipulation benchmark with diverse scripted tasks, including articulated-state interactions.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Treat it as an enabling benchmark: only methods evaluated on tasks explicitly involving articulated state should enter the articulation-specific comparison table.

benchmarks.name: BEHAVIOR-1K / OmniGibson
benchmarks.task: Long-horizon household tasks in realistic scenes using mobile, bimanual-capable embodied agents and dynamic object states.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: The 2026 challenge pins an evaluation configuration and restricts policies to onboard observations; retain version, robot configuration, task subset, and partial-credit rule with any result. OmniGibson is covered as BEHAVIOR-1K software, not as a separate misattributed paper record.

benchmarks.name: SceneFun3D
benchmarks.task: Functionality segmentation, language-driven affordance grounding, and interaction-motion annotations.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: SceneFun3D's documented segmentation/grounding evaluation uses dataset v0.2.0 and hidden test submissions. Segmentation is ranked by AP averaged over IoU thresholds; grounding by AP50. For scene-level motion estimation, see the Articulate3D challenge. Keep the datasets, inputs, and scoring protocols distinct.
unresolved_entries: Revisit the dynamic EvalAI table before identifying current leaders or associating submission names with papers.

benchmarks.name: Articulate3D Challenge
benchmarks.task: Scene-level movable-part and interactable-region segmentation, with motion type, axis and origin prediction.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: The ECCV 2026 page specifies indoor scene point clouds and reports segmentation AP50 together with motion metrics MA, MO and MAO-ST. Keep challenge editions separate, and distinguish this motion-estimation protocol from SceneFun3D segmentation and grounding evaluation.
unresolved_entries: Resolve other named challenge submissions to their official papers before adding publication records.

benchmarks.name: RoboCasa / RoboCasa365
benchmarks.task: Generalist kitchen manipulation with mobile robots, articulated appliances and composite household tasks.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: The current multi-task leaderboard evaluates 50 target tasks with Atomic-Seen, Composite-Seen and Composite-Unseen splits; its specified pretraining data and versioned horizons matter. Distinguish original RoboCasa from RoboCasa365 and model versions from the publications introducing their families.
unresolved_entries: Many current policy submissions and agentic wrappers have not yet been mapped to individual canonical papers. The listed policy records are contextual references only; they do not assert an exact submitted configuration, score, or rank.

benchmarks.name: ALFRED
benchmarks.task: Language-guided household task completion with navigation and object interaction in AI2-THOR.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Record seen/unseen split, task type, observation setup, and whether language subgoals are provided.

benchmarks.name: TEACh
benchmarks.task: Dialog-guided embodied household tasks with an interactive teacher in AI2-THOR.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Keep dialog setting, task split, and agent interaction budget alongside results.

benchmarks.name: OpenEQA
benchmarks.task: Open-vocabulary embodied question answering from episodic memory or active exploration.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Distinguish episodic-memory and active-exploration settings; natural-language answers use the benchmark evaluation protocol.

benchmarks.name: EmbodiedQA
benchmarks.task: Navigation and question answering in 3D environments.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Treat navigation budget and answer accuracy as linked but separate aspects of the task.

benchmarks.name: Habitat 2.0 / Home Assistant Benchmark
benchmarks.task: Physics-enabled household rearrangement and home-assistant tasks in interactive 3D environments.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Preserve task, robot embodiment, controller, observations, and generalization split when comparing agents.

benchmarks.name: Habitat 3.0
benchmarks.task: Collaborative social navigation and social rearrangement with humanoid avatars or human partners.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: State whether evaluation uses avatar policies or humans-in-the-loop, plus task and environment setting.

benchmarks.name: GOAT-Bench
benchmarks.task: Lifelong navigation to object-category, image, and language goals.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Preserve goal modality, memory setting, noise configuration, and lifelong episode structure.

benchmarks.name: Room-to-Room (R2R)
benchmarks.task: Vision-and-language navigation in real scanned indoor environments.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Record split, navigation metric, instruction setting, and scene dataset/version.

benchmarks.name: Habitat navigation ecosystem
benchmarks.task: Embodied navigation with simulation, scene datasets, sensors, and task configurations.
benchmarks.protocol_notes: Navigation papers use differing scene datasets, goal specifications, maps, and sensing; do not compare them without those fields.
